VeraGridEngine.Simulations.LinearFactors.linear_analysis.compute_phase_shift_terms(nc: NumericalCircuit) → Tuple[ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]]][source]

Build the per-unit contribution of the branch phase shifts to the DC branch flows.

A branch with susceptance b = 1 / (X · m) and phase shift tau has Pf = b · (theta_f - theta_t - tau). This is the same convention as compute_linear_admittances and power_flow_post_process_linear. The tap ratio is t = m · exp(j · tau), so both the tap module and the tap phase enter the DC flow.

Separating the constant part turns the DC system into B·theta = P - Pshift, so the flows are Pf = PTDF @ (P - Pshift) + shift_flow with shift_flow = -b·tau and Pshift[from] = -b·tau, Pshift[to] = +b·tau. Without these two terms the PTDF flows are simply blind to any phase shifter.

Parameters:

nc – numerical circuit

Returns:

direct flow term per branch, equivalent bus injections, in p.u.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.LinearFactors.linear_analysis.make_dP_from_bus_types(bus_types: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[int64]], distribute_slack: bool) → ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | ndarray[tuple[int, int], dtype[float64]][source]

Build the dP / Dij matrix used to modify the PTDF.

bus_types:

1 -> PQ 2 -> PV 3 -> Slack

If distribute_slack=True:

The balancing injection is distributed equally among PV + Slack buses.

P_eff = dP @ P P_eff = P - w * sum(P)

If distribute_slack=False:

Return identity, preserving the current single-slack PTDF behavior.
